reviews.identity_notes: Vinhedo 3 is a new single-tenant AI data center on Ascenty's existing Vinhedo campus (Av. Joao Batista Nunes 50, Distrito Industrial Benedito Storani, Vinhedo SP). That campus already runs Vinhedo 1 (2019) and Vinhedo 2 (2020). Vinhedo 3 was announced on 27-28 May 2026 within a US$1.2bn program covering Sumare 3, the Vinhedo 2 expansion (50 to 80 MW), Vinhedo 3, and Vinhedo 4 and 5 (45 MW each, pre-construction). Sources disagree on capacity: 90 MW in Ascenty's English release, Bloomberg Linea and DCD; 80 MW in the Portuguese and Spanish versions, IT Forum, Teletime and InvestNews; Baguete gives '90 MW, 60 MW para uso e 30 MW de TI'. Two outlets used future-tense or ambiguous wording ('planeja ... construir o campus Vinhedo 3' in Teletime; 'terá' in Telesintese). The first-party release, Bloomberg Linea, IT Forum and TI Inside say it is being built now. A 2020 brochure grouped 'Vinhedo 3 to 5' at 44 MW combined, so the current Vinhedo 3 is a resized successor plan. Do not confuse it with Sumare 3, where works started in March 2026. The in-window determination rests mainly on the company's own present-tense statement of 28 May 2026. Satellite imagery dated 2026-07-15 corroborates it: new earthworks and grading on the parcel next to the campus, not present on 2025-09-30. No independent on-site report names Vinhedo 3 at a specific physical stage, so confidence is moderate, not high.

reviews.identity_notes:
- Naming: BER02 is maincubes' name for the first data center (of up to six) on its Nauen campus, which it also calls 'mainHub Berlin' or the 'mainHub-Campus'. The campus is about 14 ha on Berliner Strasse in 14641 Nauen (Havelland, Brandenburg), at the south-east town entrance, east of the B5/B273 and south of Gewerbegebiet Nauen-Ost.
- Land and planning: maincubes bought the land in October 2024. The planning basis is the Stadt Nauen B-Plan 'Rechenzentrum'; the Satzungsfassung is dated Dec 2024 and the plan became legally binding on 2 July 2025. The plan's stormwater concept names AM:PM Grund Alpha GmbH as client.
- Works: groundbreaking for the 110 kV substation and the ~6 km cable route to the E.DIS grid was on 24 March 2026, with JSM Group as general contractor. The physical works I can show in the window are this campus substation and site infrastructure, not the BER02 data-hall building itself.
- Do not confuse with the separate eastern 'Sondergebiet Rechenzentrum 2' B-Plan (formerly 'Gewerbegebiet Nauen Sued-Ost'). Its draft was on public display 16.06-20.07.2026 and it is described as still farmland (Stadt Nauen notice, captured as nauen-pm-rz2-2026.pdf, sha256 875fa3171221d83d8f1fb290376aa829d1b1c04dc7014befc3f2684adcbfe4e4).
- Capacity figures disagree between sources: 200 MW grid link expandable to 400 MW, versus 144-186 MW IT on the operator page.
- RFS has moved from 12/2027 to Q3/2028.
- No official 2026 aerial photo is available yet. The LGB 2026 flight for Los 13 'Oranienburg' was flown on 22 April, before the window, and is not yet published; the current DOP tile 33357-5829 dates from 14.05.2024 (captured as lgb-bildflugstand-2026-site.xml and lgb-dop-aktualitaet-site.xml). So the in-window physical evidence rests on Copernicus Sentinel-2 imagery. I interpreted that imagery myself, matched against the B-Plan's designated substation location and the contractor's 21 May statement.

reviews.identity_notes:
'TRG HOU2' is TRG Datacenters' second data center building on its Houston campus at 2626 Spring Cypress Road, Spring, TX 77388, in unincorporated Harris County. Some press spell it 'Spring Cyprus'. The campus name 'TRG Spring Cypress Campus' matches this site; TRG calls it its Houston campus.

- **Owner and sponsor:** the land owner of record is Technical Realty Group of Texas, LLC, both at HCAD and TDLR. TRG has been backed by Tallvine Partners since August 2025.
- **Size and phasing:** TRG markets 'HOU2 & 3' as up to 24 MW and 110,000 GSF at full build-out. Its page lists '45K Facility GSF' and a first phase in Q4 2026. The July 2026 brochure gives HOU2 at 2.25 MW from Q4 2026 and HOU3 at up to 15 MW from Q4 2027 as a direct two-story extension of HOU2.
- **TDLR filing:** the TDLR TABS filing 'TRG Datacenters Phase 3' (TABS2026004413) covers a new 38,729 sf building costing $6,645,330. It is evidently the HOU2 first-phase building. 'Phase 3' is campus numbering after HOU1 Phase 1 (2018) and Phase 2 (2021). Community Impact's '$6.6M' figure matches this filing rather than the full 24 MW cost.
- **Footprint:** TRG's July 2026 site-layout image places HOU2 NW of HOU1 in line with it, with HOU3 beside HOU2 on the field side. This matches where Sentinel-2 shows new construction inside the parcel.
- **Imagery caveats:** the Sentinel-2 evidence is 10 m imagery interpreted by the reviewer. It shows a new structure in the HOU2 position on four clear in-window dates, but cannot by itself show interior work. The in-window 'under construction' reading rests on that physical presence combined with the operator's in-window statement (2026-07-22) that HOU2 is still to be delivered in Q4 2026. The 2026-05-30 scene was cloud-contaminated over the site. The main brightening happened between 2026-05-12 (before the window) and 2026-06-29 (in the window), so it cannot be dated precisely to inside the window.
- **Other captures:** the 2026/01 'TRG-Campus-HOU2-Brochure.pdf' URL now redirects to the July 2026 brochure (identical sha256). Esri World Imagery Wayback metadata shows the newest high-resolution capture there is 2025-11-26, before the window, so it was not used.

location.method:

reviews.identity_notes: 'Amazon Falls Township Innovation Campus' corresponds to AWS's 'Falls Township Innovation Campus at Keystone Trade Center', the title of Amazon's 2026-07-14 PADEP public meeting presentation. It is one of the first two campuses named in Amazon's June 2025 announcement of at least $20B in Pennsylvania. The permittee is Amazon Data Services Inc (DEP plant 'AMAZON DATA SVCS INC PNE100', plan approvals 09-0261 issued 2025-07-25 and 09-0261A proposed). The site is about 250 acres within NorthPoint Development's Keystone Trade Center on the former U.S. Steel Fairless Works, Falls Township, Bucks County, PA. The facility address is 600 Ben Fairless Drive (mailing city Morrisville, 19067). A June 2025 Falls Township article mentioned '1 Ben Fairless Drive, where building six will become a data center'. The later DEP documents use 600 Ben Fairless Drive, and the county's 600 address point falls in the NP Keystone Bldg 6 parcel, so I used the DEP address. Plans call for about 10 buildings and 2 to 3 million sq ft built in phases. The initial building is about 1M sq ft. Phase 1 has 72 diesel critical engines plus 4 house engines, installed from September 2025 and operating or testing since April 2026. Phase 2 (280 gas engines) was still in permitting as of 2026-08-20. This review covers the campus buildout as a whole, which was clearly active in the window. Even if parts of the first building were being commissioned, the buildout was not complete. The NPDES construction stormwater permit PAD090088 A-3 for 'Keystone Trade Center-Area 3 Development Part A.3' (NP Falls Township Ind LLC) was also captured as context (dep-npdes-pad090088). It contained no coordinates.

successor_check.notes:
I searched for completion, opening, pause, halt, stop-work and cancellation reports for the Prologis Trenton (Project Mila) campus through 2026-08-20 and found none.

- Pre-window context from search results (not captured): in March 2026, coverage said grading for the on-site substation was underway, and Prologis said that did not mean vertical construction had begun. The first building was targeted for 2028 and full buildout for 2029.
- Status during and after the window:
  - 2026-07-09: Trenton council approved the 15-year, 75% Community Reinvestment Area (CRA) abatement.
  - 2026-08-03: council declined to certify the residents' charter-amendment petition.
  - 2026-09-01: the Ohio Supreme Court ordered the petition certified, and Issue 17 went on the 2026-11-03 ballot. That is after the window, and organizers say it would not stop the already-approved Prologis project.
  - September 2026: the city's separate 601-acre annexation for a different AWS project was withdrawn. That is a different project, not this campus.
- No authoritative source reports this project as completed, opened or cancelled on or before 2026-08-20. Planned operation is 2028–2029, so completion within the window is implausible.

Caveat: the turn's web-search budget ran out near the end of the review, so I could not run a final search of Journal-News or Trenton council minutes for June–August 2026. Findings rest on the searches already completed.

- Steps: I took the parcel ring in its native coordinates and computed the polygon area centroid in projected coordinates: X 1415463.86 ftUS, Y 535915.27 ftUS. The centroid falls inside the polygon. I then inverse-projected it with my own EPSG:3735 Lambert Conformal Conic 2SP implementation on GRS80.
- Cross-check: the server's own outSR=4326 geometry gives a centroid of -84.458780, 39.454958, about 1 m away.
- Parcel figures: the ring area is 6,444,950 sq ftUS, or 147.96 acres. The bounding box is lon -84.46497 to -84.44896 and lat 39.45049 to 39.45983.
- Ownership: the Butler County Auditor record for R8000060000011 confirms the owner, records a 19-MAR-2026 transfer, and gives the mailing address 1800 Wazee St Ste 500, Denver CO 80202. That is Prologis's Denver office address per public directory and trademark listings found in search, which I did not capture.
- Lineage: the 2023 Ohio statewide parcel layer (ODNR) shows the same footprint as three City of Trenton parcels (R8000060000005, -06 and -07, 146.5 assessed acres in total). This is consistent with the October 2025 city-to-Prologis sale and a 2026 consolidation.

location.method:
Butler County Engineer's Office public parcel layer, gismaps.bceo.org Public/ParcelQuery FeatureServer layer 0 'CURRENTPARCELS'. I queried PIN R8000060000011, owned by TRENTON DATA CENTER CAMPUS LLC on Arnold Brown Industrial Dr in the Trenton Corp tax district.

I then inverse-projected it with my own EPSG:3735 Lambert Conformal Conic 2SP implementation on GRS80.
- Cross-check: the server's own outSR=4326 geometry gives a centroid of -84.458780, 39.454958, about 1 m away.
- Parcel figures: the ring area is 6,444,950 sq ftUS, or 147.96 acres. The bounding box is lon -84.46497 to -84.44896 and lat 39.45049 to 39.45983.
- Ownership: the Butler County Auditor record for R8000060000011 confirms the owner, records a 19-MAR-2026 transfer, and gives the mailing address 1800 Wazee St Ste 500, Denver CO 80202. That is Prologis's Denver office address per public directory and trademark listings found in search, which I did not capture.

location.source_crs_and_transformation:

reviews.identity_notes:
The named project is the new-build Technologiezentrum Laufenburg (TZL) of the FlexBase Group in Laufenburg AG, Switzerland. ERNE AG, which is based in Laufenburg, is general contractor and Frei Architekten is the architect. It is being built on the former Swissgrid site 'across from the existing structure'. That existing structure is the revitalised building at Werkstrasse 12 (EGID 585249), which the project overview says will provide more than 400 office workplaces.

The campus therefore covers both the existing building and the new build. I placed the point on the new build, because that is the building under construction.

Key dates and parties:
- Groundbreaking: 5 May 2025.
- Cornerstone: Friday 29 May 2026, in the 27 m deep pit.
- Construction approval: April 2025.
- Flow-battery partner announced 21 May 2026: Invinity.

The figures differ by source:
- Battery: ERNE says >500 MW; other press says 1.2 GW and 1.6 GW/2.1 GWh.
- AI data centre: 480 MW, per secondary trade press (Baxtel).
- Building volume: 864,000 m³ (AZ/NFZ), 'almost 900,000 m³' (ERNE), 709,000 m³ in the GWR record.

None of these differences affect identity.

Register details:
- The GWR record's building class code is 1220 (office building) and its status code is 1001 (planned). Both lag the physical reality.
- The GWR parcel number 2935 and the cadastral map number 2682 share the same EGRID, CH671688837410.
- Per SRF, the canton has approved only the building shell, and the battery is still under environmental review.

Baxtel (16 May 2026) and bebeez (15 May 2026) report the start of works but fall before the window, so I did not rely on them.

reviewer_output.identity_notes:
The named project is the new-build Technologiezentrum Laufenburg (TZL) of the FlexBase Group in Laufenburg AG, Switzerland. ERNE AG, which is based in Laufenburg, is general contractor and Frei Architekten is the architect. It is being built on the former Swissgrid site 'across from the existing structure'. That existing structure is the revitalised building at Werkstrasse 12 (EGID 585249), which the project overview says will provide more than 400 office workplaces.

The campus therefore covers both the existing building and the new build. I placed the point on the new build, because that is the building under construction.

Key dates and parties:
- Groundbreaking: 5 May 2025.
- Cornerstone: Friday 29 May 2026, in the 27 m deep pit.
- Construction approval: April 2025.
- Flow-battery partner announced 21 May 2026: Invinity.

The figures differ by source:
- Battery: ERNE says >500 MW; other press says 1.2 GW and 1.6 GW/2.1 GWh.
- AI data centre: 480 MW, per secondary trade press (Baxtel).
- Building volume: 864,000 m³ (AZ/NFZ), 'almost 900,000 m³' (ERNE), 709,000 m³ in the GWR record.

None of these differences affect identity.

Register details:
- The GWR record's building class code is 1220 (office building) and its status code is 1001 (planned). Both lag the physical reality.
- The GWR parcel number 2935 and the cadastral map number 2682 share the same EGRID, CH671688837410.
- Per SRF, the canton has approved only the building shell, and the battery is still under environmental review.

Baxtel (16 May 2026) and bebeez (15 May 2026) report the start of works but fall before the window, so I did not rely on them.

(b) The 2019 announcement of a 16 MW building 'on the opposite plot' was the earlier Lupfig expansion (Lupin 3). A first-party press release (2026-07-14) supports it, but says only 'zwei weitere sind im Bau' without naming DC4. I found no in-window dated site photo or site-visit report. The latest SWISSIMAGE aerial for this tile is from 2024, before the window. Even so, the in-window statements, the late-2025 physical stage (finished shell, MEP under way) and the post-window 'still under construction, opening early 2027' status all point the same way: work was under way during the window. On location: the GWR record for EGID 192064212 still shows status 'approved' (1002) rather than 'under construction' (1003). That is register lag; I did not use it as construction evidence. reviews.identity_notes:
The project is Hyperco Oy's data centre at the Loviisa Eastern Junction (Itäinen liittymä / Östra anslutningen), Kuningattarenranta district 10, block 1064 (renumbered from 1045 by plan 10-30).

How the campus was assembled:
- The City of Loviisa ran a land tender on 16–31.12.2024. Bids came from SRV Oy and Hyperco Oy, and Hyperco won.
- The Näringslivs- och infrastrukturnämnd reserved about 26 ha for Hyperco on 30.01.2025 §7 (building right 105,800 m²-vy). Capture: loviisa-kokous-2025969-7.pdf.
- On 28.08.2025 §126 the same board, followed by the City Board on 08.09.2025 §299, proposed a 50-year lease of the 26 ha with a purchase option. Capture: loviisa-kokous-20251163-5.pdf.
- Plan 10-30, approved 25.09.2025, rezoned the block to T-5, which explicitly allows data centre buildings. It created plot 1 (city land) and plot 2 (state land, 6.66 ha).
- Metsähallitus leased the 6.6 ha state plot to Hyperco, announced 2026-06-04, describing it as 'next to' the project Hyperco launched in 2025.
- The city's 2025-01-27 notice links the project to Fingrid's planned Skogbacka substation and gives a preliminary commissioning date of 2027–2028.
- Loviisan Sanomat reported on 2025-12-22 (headline and lead only, paywalled, not captured) that the first Itäinen liittymä data centre had received a building permit and that the forest had already been felled.

Earthworks contractor: Kreate Oy.

Different project, not to be confused: Nova Complex (Singapore) is building a separate data centre at the same junction. Its 6 ha city plot lies north of Pietarintie (road 170), and Kaivuupalvelu Finer Oy started rock excavation there on 9.3.2026 (city notice 2026-03-05; Itäväylä 2026-03-09). Those Nova Complex works are not evidence for Hyperco. The Hyperco evidence I used names Hyperco explicitly and places the works south of Ohikulkutie/VT7.

Plot centroids, for reference: plot 1 at 60.473823 N, 26.271194 E; plot 2 at 60.475697 N, 26.276687 E.

location.method: I took the official parcel polygon from the State of Colorado OIT statewide public parcel service, which aggregates county assessor parcels: Douglas County parcel_id 223305207007, account R0626486, situs '15255 COMPARK BLVD', owner 'FLEXENTIAL CORP', legal description 'LOT 1 COMPARK VILLAGE 13 16.813 AM/L', land use Industrial, received 4/21/2026. It matches Flexential's first-party address, 15255 Compark Blvd, Parker, CO 80134, and the 17-acre site size. I computed the area-weighted polygon centroid from the 23-vertex ring in a local equirectangular plane; the computed area is about 16.67 acres. The point is inside the polygon. As an independent check, the Town of Parker development-tour point for SP24-114 'Compark Village F13 L1 - Data Center' (-104.810857, 39.560374) falls inside the same parcel, about 29 m from the centroid. location.source_crs_and_transformation: The service and query output use EPSG:4326 (WGS84 geographic, spatialReference wkid 4326, requested with outSR=4326). I applied no datum transformation. The county source data is NAD83-based and the state service publishes it in 4326; any residual NAD83/WGS84 offset is about 1 m and does not matter here. I computed the centroid myself with a local planar approximation (cos(lat)-scaled degrees) and converted it back to degrees.
location.what_the_point_represents: The centroid of the Douglas County assessor parcel (Lot 1, Compark Village Filing 13) owned by Flexential Corp at 15255 Compark Blvd. This is the Flexential Parker data center campus site, at the corner of Chambers Road and Compark Blvd.

reviews.identity_notes:
Delta Forge 1 is Applied Digital's AI Factory campus at Boyce, Rapides Parish, Louisiana. The company named Boyce in its 2026-07-27 FY2026 results, and its 2026-10-07 Q1 FY2027 release places DF1 in Louisiana and DF2 in Alabama.

What the sources say about the project:
- Scope: two 150 MW buildings (DF1-1 and DF1-2), 300 MW critical IT load out of 430 MW utility power. Leased on about 15-year terms to a high investment-grade US hyperscaler through subsidiaries APLD AEX-01 LLC and APLD AEX-02 LLC (leases dated 2026-04-20 and 2026-04-22).
- Local identifiers: the incentive term sheet calls it 'Project Lightning'. The site lies in England District Sub-District No. 4, on a 672.52-acre tract Applied Digital bought in December 2025. Local press says about 300 acres are announced for the two buildings; the OSM fenced construction zone is about 535 acres.
- Permits and utilities: LDEQ construction stormwater coverage LAR10Q714 names the site '5941 LA Hwy 121, Boyce' with Beard Construction Group LLC (an organisation, not an individual). Cleco will serve the site over a 230 kV line.

Timeline caveats:
- The company announced a groundbreaking on 2026-01-22 without naming the state.
- Local officials still called it a 'prospect' in February to April 2026.
- Governor Landry formally announced it on 2026-05-26.
- Physical work is documented from April 2026 (stormwater coverage effective 2026-04-02, wells drilled 2026-04-09 to 2026-04-21) through the window. KALB had already labelled the 2026-05-26 event a 'groundbreaking'. The LDEQ dust citation followed on 2026-05-27 and the construction imagery dates from 2026-07-30.

Do not confuse DF1 with Delta Forge 2 (210 MW, Alabama, leased 2026-06-05) or with the Polaris Forge campuses in North Dakota.

Evidence limits:
- I could not open primary LDEQ, LPSC and Scribd-hosted documents: LDEQ and LPSC sit behind Cloudflare and Scribd behind a JS challenge, and I did not try to bypass them. The LDEQ citation therefore rests on KALB's reporting.
- The Kingfish source is affiliated with the OSM editor of the site polygon and worked with an advocacy group, so I treat it only as corroboration.

reviewer_output.identity_notes:
Delta Forge 1 is Applied Digital's AI Factory campus at Boyce, Rapides Parish, Louisiana. The company named Boyce in its 2026-07-27 FY2026 results, and its 2026-10-07 Q1 FY2027 release places DF1 in Louisiana and DF2 in Alabama.

What the sources say about the project:
- Scope: two 150 MW buildings (DF1-1 and DF1-2), 300 MW critical IT load out of 430 MW utility power. Leased on about 15-year terms to a high investment-grade US hyperscaler through subsidiaries APLD AEX-01 LLC and APLD AEX-02 LLC (leases dated 2026-04-20 and 2026-04-22).
- Local identifiers: the incentive term sheet calls it 'Project Lightning'. The site lies in England District Sub-District No. 4, on a 672.52-acre tract Applied Digital bought in December 2025. Local press says about 300 acres are announced for the two buildings; the OSM fenced construction zone is about 535 acres.
- Permits and utilities: LDEQ construction stormwater coverage LAR10Q714 names the site '5941 LA Hwy 121, Boyce' with Beard Construction Group LLC (an organisation, not an individual). Cleco will serve the site over a 230 kV line.

Timeline caveats:
- The company announced a groundbreaking on 2026-01-22 without naming the state.
- Local officials still called it a 'prospect' in February to April 2026.
- Governor Landry formally announced it on 2026-05-26.
- Physical work is documented from April 2026 (stormwater coverage effective 2026-04-02, wells drilled 2026-04-09 to 2026-04-21) through the window. KALB had already labelled the 2026-05-26 event a 'groundbreaking'. The LDEQ dust citation followed on 2026-05-27 and the construction imagery dates from 2026-07-30.

Do not confuse DF1 with Delta Forge 2 (210 MW, Alabama, leased 2026-06-05) or with the Polaris Forge campuses in North Dakota.

- I could not open primary LDEQ, LPSC and Scribd-hosted documents: LDEQ and LPSC sit behind Cloudflare and Scribd behind a JS challenge, and I did not try to bypass them. The LDEQ citation therefore rests on KALB's reporting.

location.method: Official building-register point. I took the Ryhti (Syke) open_building and open_address OGC API Features records for permanent building ID 102627624H, whose official address point is 'Tehdaskatu 15', 87100 Kajaani. I chose this building because its permit history lines up with CSC's three projects in the hall. CSC says LUMI-AI is being built 'in the same hall' as the 2022 LUMI data center and the 2025 Roihu system. This building's alterations ran 2020-02-24 to 2021-05-24 (matching the LUMI data center) and 2024-11-21 to 2025-09-11 (matching Roihu), and a third alteration started on 2026-01-21 and is still in progress (matching LUMI-AI, which CSC and SRV say started in January 2026). CSC gives its Kajaani Data Center visiting address as Renforsin Ranta business area, Tehdaskatu 15, 87100 Kajaani. That address alone does not settle it, because about 70 Ryhti address points across the Renforsin Ranta mill share 'Tehdaskatu 15'. The register does not name occupants, so linking this building to CSC rests on that matching.
location.source_crs_and_transformation: The source stores the point in EPSG:3067 (ETRS89 / ETRS-TM35FIN), as shown by point_location_srid 3067. The GeoServer OGC API transforms it server-side and returns GeoJSON in EPSG:4326 / CRS84 (lon, lat). I applied no further transformation. I treated ETRS89 and WGS84 as equivalent; they differ by less than about 1 m here. The same coordinate is returned by the open_address record for 'Tehdaskatu 15' (building_key bf7a3900-78af-4af2-b119-3277d47ff7f0) and by the permit records for 2024-2026.
location.what_the_point_represents: The building register's location centre point for building 102627624H. This is the former paper machine hall at Renforsin Ranta, Kajaani (built 1980-82; 26,961 m² gross floor area; 230,830 m³). It houses CSC's Kajaani Data Center (LUMI and Roihu) and the LUMI-AI data hall now under construction. The point stands for the whole building, not the specific LUMI-AI data hall inside it.

reviewer_output.identity_notes: The project is the LUMI AI Factory data center ('LUMI-AI data center'), owned by CSC - IT Center for Science Ltd. SRV is the main contractor, and SRV's filings list it as 'Lumi AI Factory', Kajaani. The work converts an existing former paper machine hall, about 200 m long, at Renforsin Ranta, Kajaani, Finland, rather than putting up a new building. It will house the EuroHPC LUMI-AI supercomputer (Bull, EUR 387.8 million contract, deployment in H2 2027) and the LUMI-IQ quantum computer (IQM). The consortium is Finland, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Norway and Poland. CSC's blog says the existing LUMI data center (2022) and Roihu (2025) are in the same hall. The 'CSC LUMI-AI Data Center' campus is therefore the same site and building as CSC's existing Kajaani Data Center, and the point coincides with it. I tied the hall to Ryhti building 102627624H by inference from matching permit dates; the register does not name occupants. reviews.identity_notes:
The named project is the first, approved building of the DC BLOX Palm Coast cable landing station / colocation campus in Palm Coast's Town Center.

Approvals and permits:
- Single building of 33,760 sq ft per the city. Site plan sheet C-200 shows a 34,823 sq ft main building plus a 52 sq ft guard house (34,875 sq ft total), 32'-3" tall.
- Technical site plan approved by the city 11/12/2025 (APP REQ #6381). FlaglerLive reports a development order dated Oct 21, 2025.
- Building permit issued April 8, 2026. The city's file name gives permit 2025100821 at 1109 Town Center Blvd. The plan title block gives the project address as 1035 Town Center Blvd, Palm Coast FL 32164.
- Engineer: Jacobs. Applicant: Tarpon Services LLC (per FlaglerLive).
- Code names: 'Project Orchid' and 'Parakeet Gumbo'/'GUMBO'.

Land:
- Legal description: Lot 7B, a portion of Lot 7, Town Center Phase 5 (MB 36 PG 79-83), Sec 5 T12S R31E, 7.05 ac.
- Plan label: parcel ID 05-12-31-5855-00000-0070, 'DCB ORCHID, LLC'.

Size discrepancy: DC BLOX marketing describes a ~100,000 sq ft, two-building campus on 20–25 acres with 16 cable pairs and 10 MW. The city says only one building has been submitted and approved, and DC BLOX's June 2026 statement concedes the permit covers only the first building. This review covers that permitted first building.

Cables and timing: the anchor cable is Google's Sol, landing at South 6th Street in Flagler Beach. Expected operational Q1 2027 (DC BLOX).

Not reviewed: the Flagler Beach landing works (HDD conduits).

- 48 Lowe's Pl is the only new data-centre build in Etobicoke. I scanned all active permits since 2022 in grids W01 to W03 for large industrial or non-residential new builds.

- Demolition permit 23 103567 DEM: demolish the Lowe's store, proposed use 'Data Centre', with a condition referencing SA-22-110986.
- New Building permit 23 169869 BLD: 'telecommunications and data processing facility', estimated cost CAD 480,000,000, industrial GFA 24,071 m².
- Conditional permits: site servicing issued 2024-12-09 (first inspection 2025-02-12); building issued 2025-04-08.

The named project is HEL17, the second data-centre building of Microsoft 3465 Finland Oy's Hepokorpi campus in Högnäs, Espoo, next to Ring Road III.

**The permit.** On 20.3.2025 (§ 41) the Espoo Environment and Building Board granted new-building permit 2024-1349. It is addressed to 'Hepokorvenkaari 1', building site 49-65-3-1, and covers 'datakeskuksen (HEL17)', its auxiliary buildings, 13 transformers and 7 electrical containers. The board also gave the right to start works before the permit became final. Captured as espoo-ymra-2025-03-20-p41-2024-1349, sha256 57a766de185f2dc7cdd4ef70bf6bb5c185280266579354171390082d94e94b12.
- Building 1 has permanent building ID 104193806H, gross area 38,747 m², floor area 33,329 m², volume 269,938 m³ and 2 storeys.
- The decision says the plot already holds permit 2024-616 for phase 1 (HEL16), the eastern building.
- The city's news release of 21.3.2025 headlined this as the Hepokorpi data centre's second building permit, 'toinen rakennuslupa' (captured as espoo-2025-03-21-second-permit, sha256 822c1af0e7498b6482824c8ade332ed124e019540da02218b4e110e32f9bf37a).

**The rest of the campus.** The third building, HEL18, received rakentamislupa 49-2026-318 on 11.6.2026, for Hepokorvenkaari 12 on plot 49-65-2-1. That plot also holds the site base (permit 2024-928).

**Microsoft's phase 2.** Microsoft's 28.4.2026 release confirmed the phase-2 construction decision across Espoo, Kirkkonummi and Vihti. It said phase-2 permits were in hand for all three campuses and phase-2 works would start in 2026. That fits HEL17 being Espoo's phase 2.

**Earlier timeline (before the window).** Winthrop's noise-notification update of 13.5.2025 scheduled HEL17 piling for 1.11.2025–14.4.2026 on the northern plot (captured as espoo-2025-05-13-meluilmoitus-paivitysliite.pdf, sha256 1aeaa70cbc1a68c9b8a7339c9024052e40a61f909b0e331a4d4c4027a5e8a013). Winthrop's status page dated 20/02/2026 listed 'Paalutus- ja louhinta ovat käynnissä pohjoisella tontilla' (piling and excavation underway on the northern plot).

**Caveats.**
- Microsoft's May 2026 wording ('construction of the second building is beginning') is ambiguous between 'starting now' and 'about to start'. A DCD article from June 2026, which I saw only as a search snippet and could not capture (HTTP 403), paraphrased it as 'set to begin shortly'. I therefore treat the city's 11.6.2026 decision as the primary in-window evidence; it names permit 2024-1349 as under construction.
- Winthrop's 3.7.2026 status is site-wide and not specific to one building.
- The Espoo permit-reporting and inspection WFS layers (rakval, GIS:Rakennusluvat*, GIS:RakentamisluvatRaportointi*) need credentials (HTTP 401). I did not use them.
- The city's 9.6.2026 decision continuing Winthrop's noise notification for blasting, piling and crushing at Hepokorvenkaari 1 and 12 (§ 23) is no longer online; its notice page returns 404. It was not used.

- **Infostatyba record:** I captured the full record set for parcel 4174/0200:200 on 2026-10-09 (infostatyba-kadastras-4174-0200-200.json, 329 rows, sha256 1e878a1c...). It has no construction-completion act or declaration and no suspension. It contains only:

  - construction-start notice ANN2-00-260122-00189, registered 2026-01-22
  - acts SPA-00-260604-00009 and ANNPA-00-260604-00012 (2026-06-04)
  - project-version rows marked 'laukiama patvirtinimo' (awaiting approval)
- **Telia's H1 2026 interim report (published 2026-07-17):** completion is targeted for H2 2027.
- **Telia press release reported by 15min.lt/BNS on 2026-09-14** (captured 15min-2026-09-14-telia-first-stage-topping-out.html, sha256 eb329572...): 'Ant Raisteniškėse statomo pastato iškeltas vainikas, tradiciškai žymintis pagrindinių konstrukcijų darbų pabaigą' (a topping-out wreath was raised on the building under construction in Raisteniškės, traditionally marking the end of the main structural works). The project was therefore neither complete, open nor cancelled on or before 2026-08-20.

location.source_crs_and_transformation: The service returns ETRS89 geographic coordinates (urn:ogc:def:crs:EPSG::4258; GeoJSON order lon, lat). I projected the point forward with my own Krueger-series Transverse Mercator code to LKS-94 / Lithuania TM (EPSG:3346: GRS80, central meridian 24°E, k0 0.9998, false easting 500000). That gives exact integer grid coordinates N 6072437.00, E 576092.00, which is the register's native LKS-94 point. I treat ETRS89 as WGS84 and apply no further datum shift; the difference is under 1 m.

reviewer_output.identity_notes:
**What the project is.** The target is Telia Lietuva's new-build Tier III data centre near Vilnius. Telia's filings call it the 'new data center near Vilnius'. It is at Raisteniškės, beside the A2 Vilnius–Panevėžys motorway. It is distinct from Telia's existing Vilnius data centres at Žirmūnai and Naujoji Vilnia.

**Project history:**
- **2022-01-07:** Nasdaq Baltic material event (captured, sha256 00206055...). Telia bought a 2-ha plot in Raisteniškės; the investment was then EUR 10m.
- **Re-scope:** up to EUR 26m for two initial modules with more than 400 racks.
- **Construction start:** early 2026, per the H1 2026 report.
- **2026-03-04:** symbolic capsule buried, reported by BNS via tv3.lt (captured, sha256 52789b2b...). The general contractor is Conres LT.
- **2026-09-14:** topping-out.
- **BREEAM:** a 'Telia Data Centre' interim certificate, BREEAM-0119-6971, Very Good, dated 19/06/2025. The address given is Vilniaus raj. sav., LT-14180 (captured, sha256 97982042...).

**Link between the site and Telia.** The Infostatyba project 2217-01-TP is 'Sandėliavimo paskirties pastato Ukmergės g. 449, Raisteniškių vs, Avižienių sen., Vilniaus r. sav., statybos projektas'. It is on parcel 4174/0200:200, which is 19,993 m², so it matches the 2-ha plot. Its structures are a special-category storage-purpose building, a solar power plant, an above-ground reservoir for equipment cooling, an underground fire-water reservoir, utility networks and a street. Its key documents are:
- building permit LSNS-08-250114-00039, dated 2025-01-14
- construction-start notice ANN2-00-260122-00189, registered 2026-01-22
- inspection acts dated 2026-06-04

The open data do not name the builder, so the link to Telia is inferred. Five independent facts support it:
- LT-14180, the BREEAM postcode, is the Address Register postcode of Ukmergės g. 449.
- The parcel size is about 2 ha and the parcel is next to the motorway.
- The permit and start-notice dates fit Telia's own statements.
- CityNow, a third-party aggregator (captured, sha256 200d69cd...), lists 'Telia duomenų centras, Ukmergės g. 449, Statytojas Telia Lietuva'.
- Sentinel-2 shows the parcel going from vegetation in 2025 to a construction site in 2026.

**Caveats:**
- **Year field:** in the rows attached to the 2026-06-04 acts, the building carries pastatymo_metai=2026. This is an attribute of the project version, not a completion record.
- **ANNPA act:** the dataset leaves the category of act ANNPA-00-260604-00012 blank. Across the dataset this code almost always follows an ANN2 start notice (180 of 188 projects). I did not rely on it.
- **ANN2 code:** ANN2's category is also blank. I read it as a construction-start notice because its predecessor code ANN is labelled 'Pranešimas apie statybos pradžią...' and ANN2 records begin on 2024-11-04, the day the ANN records stop.
- **Village name:** the Address Register now links Ukmergės g. 449 to Klevinė village (settlement code 18119), following Vilnius district's settlement-boundary change list of July 2025 (captured vrsa PDF, sha256 0fd0a479...). Infostatyba, its street code 1510888 and the press still use Raisteniškės.
- **Sentinel-2:** the 10 m band windows were read by HTTP range requests and are not fully captured, because each file is about 200–300 MB. The SCL files and STAC items are captured.

reviewer_session_id is the session's agent ID in that journal, and session_sequence is the 1-based line number of its started event there, so it is the start order.
